## What it is

The Program Management policy states what the organization requires for program management and who is accountable for it. Its opening sections meet [PM-1](/controls/pm/pm-1/), and it adds one statement group per control. NIST SP 800-53B allocates no PM control to a security baseline: the organization carries them out once for all its systems, whatever their baselines. So this policy has one organization-wide edition, which every baseline's starter kit includes.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 35 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who leads the security program, and who approves the program plan and sets the organization's risk tolerance? | [PM-1](/controls/pm/pm-1/), [PM-2](/controls/pm/pm-2/), [PM-28](/controls/pm/pm-28/) | The Chief Information Security Officer leads the program; the senior leader approves the plan and sets risk tolerance. | Senior leader |
| Who leads the privacy program, and is it combined with another role? | [PM-18](/controls/pm/pm-18/), [PM-19](/controls/pm/pm-19/) | A senior privacy official who reports to the senior leader. A small organization may give the role to its general counsel or compliance lead. | Senior leader |
| Which PM controls do not apply, and why? | [PM-8](/controls/pm/pm-8/), [PM-17](/controls/pm/pm-17/), [PM-24](/controls/pm/pm-24/) | PM-8 applies only to owners or operators of critical infrastructure, PM-17 only where the organization holds controlled unclassified information, and PM-24 only to organizations that run matching programs. Record each decision in the program plan. | Chief Information Security Officer |

## Preview (annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-1 asks for an organization-wide information security program plan: a document that describes the program, its common controls and who is responsible for what, approved by a senior official. This policy commits the organization to that plan and sets the rules for keeping it. The plan itself is a separate document: start from the [Information Security Program Plan template](/templates/plans/information-security-program-plan/). Program management controls are carried out once for the whole organization; NIST SP 800-53B allocates none of them to a security baseline, so this policy has a single edition whatever the baselines of your systems. Each statement cites the PM-1 item it meets.
:::

### Purpose

This policy establishes <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>'s organization-wide information security program, and states who leads it and how it is planned, resourced and overseen.

### Scope

This policy applies to all of <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>: every system it owns or operates or that is operated on its behalf, the mission and business processes those systems support, and every person with access to them. The program management controls in this policy are carried out once for the organization, and systems inherit them as common controls.

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and for the information security program, and shall approve exceptions to this policy. (PM-1a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall lead the privacy program and coordinate it with the information security program. (PM-1a.3)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall use the common controls the program provides and record them as inherited in the system security plan. (PM-1a.1)
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (PM-1a.2)

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources the information security and privacy programs need. (PM-1a.2)

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate the program with the privacy, legal, human resources, procurement, finance, physical security and mission functions, and record that coordination in the program plan. (PM-1a.3)

### Compliance

- This policy and the program plan shall be consistent with the laws, regulations and standards that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (PM-1a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (PM-1a.2)
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (PM-1a.2)
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (PM-1a.2)

### Information security program plan

:::note[Guidance]
Assessors ask to see the approved plan, its approval date and evidence of the last review. A plan can be one document or a set of documents, as long as the set is identified. The plan lists the common controls the program provides, so system owners can mark them as inherited in each system security plan.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall develop, maintain and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan. (PM-1a)
- The plan shall give an overview of the requirements for the security program, and describe the program management controls and common controls in place or planned to meet them. (PM-1a.1)
- The plan shall identify and assign roles and responsibilities, and describe management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance. (PM-1a.2)
- The plan shall reflect the coordination among the organizational entities responsible for information security. (PM-1a.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span>, as the senior official accountable for the risk the organization incurs, shall approve the plan. (PM-1a.4)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall disseminate the approved plan to every system owner and authorizing official and to the leaders of the functions named under Coordination. (PM-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update the plan <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review and update the organization-wide information security program plan <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that trigger the review and update of the organization-wide information security program plan <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a significant change to the organization's mission, structure, risk tolerance or systems, a major incident, or a finding from an assessment or audit of the program</span></span>. (PM-1b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification by limiting who can change it and keeping each approved version. (PM-1c)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one program management control or enhancement. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets. Where a control does not apply to your organization, keep its heading, replace the statements with the reason, and record the decision in the program plan.
:::

#### Information security program leadership role (PM-2)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-2 asks for one named senior official who owns the security program. Assessors look for the appointment in writing (a delegation memo or charter) and for evidence that the official has budget and staff, not just a title.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall appoint a <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> to coordinate, develop, implement and maintain the organization-wide information security program. (PM-2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall record the appointment in writing and give the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> the mission and resources the role needs. (PM-2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

FISMA requires the agency head to designate a senior agency information security officer who has information security duties as that official's primary duty ([44 U.S.C. § 3554(a)(3)(A)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim)).

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall be the senior agency information security officer the agency head designates under 44 U.S.C. § 3554(a)(3)(A), with information security duties as that official's primary duty. (PM-2)

</div>

#### Information security and privacy resources (PM-3)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-3 ties the programs to the budget. Evidence is the security and privacy line items in each capital planning or investment request, and a record of any request that left them out and why.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall identify the resources the information security and privacy programs need, for each capital planning and investment request. (PM-3a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall include those resources in capital planning and investment requests, and document every exception. (PM-3a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall prepare the security and privacy documentation that capital planning and investment requests require under applicable laws, regulations, policies and standards. (PM-3b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall make the planned information security and privacy resources available for expenditure. (PM-3c)

#### Plan of action and milestones process (PM-4)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-4 is the organization-level process; CA-5 is each system's plan of action and milestones (POA&M). Use one format across systems, such as the [POA&M template](/templates/forms/plan-of-action-and-milestones/), so the program can roll items up and compare them against the risk management strategy.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall maintain a process that ensures plans of action and milestones are developed and maintained for the information security, privacy and supply chain risk management programs and for each organizational system. (PM-4a.1)
- Each plan of action and milestones shall document the remedial actions planned to respond to risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations and the Nation. (PM-4a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall report plans of action and milestones to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: how often, for example quarterly</span>, and to regulators and customers as laws and contracts require. (PM-4a.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review plans of action and milestones for consistency with the risk management strategy and the organization-wide priorities for risk response. (PM-4b)

#### System inventory (PM-5)

:::note[Guidance]
The system inventory is the list of systems the program is responsible for: each with an owner, a categorization, an authorization status and its boundary. CM-8 is the component inventory inside each system. Start from the [System Inventory template](/templates/forms/system-inventory/). An assessor compares the inventory with the authorization records, so keep both in step.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall maintain an inventory of organizational systems and update it <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to update the inventory of organizational systems <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly, and whenever a system is authorized, significantly changed or retired</span></span>. (PM-5)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall add a system to the inventory before it is authorized or placed in operation. (PM-5)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

The Paperwork Reduction Act requires each agency head to maintain an inventory of major information systems, updated at least annually ([44 U.S.C. § 3505(c)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3505&num=0&edition=prelim)).

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall update the inventory at least annually and whenever the agency adds, significantly changes or retires a major information system. (PM-5)

</div>

#### Inventory of personally identifiable information (PM-5(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall establish, maintain and update <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to update the inventory of systems, applications, and projects that process personally identifiable information <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least annually, and whenever a privacy impact assessment is completed or updated</span></span> an inventory of all systems, applications and projects that process personally identifiable information. (PM-5(1))

#### Measures of performance (PM-6)

:::note[Guidance]
Choose a few measures that show whether the programs work, such as the share of systems with a current authorization, overdue plan of action items, and remediation within the required times. Report the same measures each period so trends show.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall develop, monitor and report on measures of performance for the information security program. (PM-6)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop, monitor and report on measures of performance for the privacy program. (PM-6)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall report the results to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span>. (PM-6)

#### Enterprise architecture (PM-7)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure the enterprise architecture is developed and maintained with consideration for information security, privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations and the Nation. (PM-7)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall review changes to the enterprise architecture that affect the processing of personally identifiable information. (PM-7)

#### Offloading (PM-7(1))

- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall offload <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: non-essential functions or services to be offloaded <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: non-essential services, such as email, file sharing and public web hosting, on systems that support mission-essential functions</span></span> to other systems, system components or an external provider. (PM-7(1))

#### Critical infrastructure plan (PM-8)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-8 applies where the organization owns or operates critical infrastructure or key resources, or helps protect them. If it does neither, keep the heading and record that decision in the program plan.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall address information security and privacy issues when the organization develops, documents and updates its critical infrastructure and key resources protection plan. (PM-8)

#### Risk management strategy (PM-9)

:::note[Guidance]
The risk management strategy says how the organization frames, assesses, responds to and monitors risk, including its risk tolerance (PM-28). Every authorization decision should be traceable to it. Start from the [Risk Management Strategy template](/templates/plans/risk-management-strategy/).
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall develop an organization-wide risk management strategy for security risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations and the Nation from the operation and use of organizational systems. (PM-9a.1)
- The strategy shall also address privacy risk to individuals from the authorized processing of personally identifiable information, developed with the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span>. (PM-9a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall approve the strategy. (PM-9a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall implement the strategy consistently across the organization. (PM-9b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update the strategy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review and update the risk management strategy <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>, and whenever organizational changes require it. (PM-9c)

#### Authorization process (PM-10)

:::note[Guidance]
PM-10 makes authorization an organization-wide process rather than a one-off per system. The program plan should name who may serve as an authorizing official and how their decisions feed the risk management strategy.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall manage the security and privacy state of organizational systems, and the environments they operate in, through an authorization process. (PM-10a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall designate the individuals who fill the roles in the risk management process, including an authorizing official for each system. (PM-10b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall integrate the authorization process into the organization-wide risk management program. (PM-10c)

#### Mission and business process definition (PM-11)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall ensure the organization's mission and business processes are defined with consideration for information security, privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations and the Nation. (PM-11a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall determine the information protection and personally identifiable information processing needs that arise from those processes. (PM-11b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall review and revise the mission and business processes <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review and revise the mission and business processes <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually, and whenever the organization changes its mission, structure or major services</span></span>. (PM-11c)

#### Insider threat program (PM-12)

:::note[Guidance]
An insider threat program brings together information that security, human resources, legal and privacy each hold, so that concerning behavior is noticed and handled consistently. Involve the privacy official from the start: the program handles personal information about the workforce.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall implement an insider threat program. (PM-12)
- The program shall include a cross-discipline insider threat incident handling team, with members from at least security, human resources, legal and privacy. (PM-12)

<!-- TODO(verify): federal block for PM-12. Executive Order 13587 (October 7, 2011) and the National Insider Threat Policy and Minimum Standards (November 2012) set the federal program; confirm both are still in effect as of 2026 at a primary source before citing them. -->

#### Security and privacy workforce (PM-13)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> and the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall establish a security and privacy workforce development and improvement program. (PM-13)
- The program shall define the knowledge and skills each security and privacy role needs, and the training and development that build them. (PM-13)

#### Testing, training and monitoring (PM-14)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall maintain a process that ensures the organization's plans for security and privacy testing, training and monitoring of organizational systems are developed and maintained. (PM-14a.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall track that those plans continue to be carried out. (PM-14a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review the testing, training and monitoring plans for consistency with the risk management strategy and the organization-wide priorities for risk response. (PM-14b)

#### Security and privacy groups and associations (PM-15)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish and maintain contact with selected security and privacy groups and associations, and record which ones. (PM-15)
- The organization shall use those contacts to support ongoing security and privacy education and training for its personnel. (PM-15a)
- The organization shall use those contacts to stay current with recommended security and privacy practices, techniques and technologies. (PM-15b)
- The organization shall use those contacts to share current security and privacy information, including threats, vulnerabilities and incidents. (PM-15c)

#### Threat awareness program (PM-16)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall implement a threat awareness program. (PM-16)
- The program shall include a capability to share threat intelligence with other organizations. (PM-16)

#### Automated means for sharing threat intelligence (PM-16(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall use automated mechanisms to share threat intelligence, such as machine-readable feeds exchanged with sharing partners. (PM-16(1))

#### Protecting controlled unclassified information on external systems (PM-17)

:::note[Guidance]
Controlled unclassified information (CUI) is information the U.S. government creates or owns that a law, regulation or government-wide policy requires to be protected. PM-17 applies wherever the organization shares CUI with external systems, or holds CUI under a contract or agreement. If it handles no CUI, keep the heading and record that decision in the program plan.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish policy and procedures to ensure that requirements for protecting controlled unclassified information processed, stored or transmitted on external systems are implemented in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, policies and standards. (PM-17a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update that policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review and update the policy <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>. (PM-17b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update those procedures <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review and update the procedures <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>. (PM-17b)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

Agencies must require non-federal systems that handle CUI to protect it with NIST SP 800-171, which [32 CFR 2002.14(h)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-32/subtitle-B/chapter-XX/part-2002/subpart-A/section-2002.14) incorporates by reference. [NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/171/r3/final) (May 2024) is the current revision, as of September 2026.

- Each agreement that shares CUI with a non-federal organization shall require the recipient to protect it as 32 CFR 2002.14(h) requires. (PM-17a)

</div>

#### Privacy program plan (PM-18)

:::note[Guidance]
The privacy program plan is the privacy counterpart of the information security program plan (PM-1). Many organizations keep them as two chapters of one program document; assessors accept that if each chapter meets its own control.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop and disseminate an organization-wide privacy program plan that gives an overview of the privacy program. (PM-18a)
- The plan shall describe the structure of the privacy program and the resources dedicated to it. (PM-18a.1)
- The plan shall give an overview of the requirements for the privacy program, and describe the privacy program management controls and common controls in place or planned to meet them. (PM-18a.2)
- The plan shall include the role of the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span>, and identify the roles and responsibilities of other privacy officials and staff. (PM-18a.3)
- The plan shall describe management commitment, compliance, and the strategic goals and objectives of the privacy program. (PM-18a.4)
- The plan shall reflect coordination among the organizational entities responsible for the different aspects of privacy. (PM-18a.5)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span>, as the senior official accountable for the privacy risk the organization incurs, shall approve the plan. (PM-18a.6)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall update the plan <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency of updates to the privacy program plan <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>, and to address changes in privacy law and policy, organizational changes, and problems found during plan implementation or privacy control assessments. (PM-18b)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

[OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix II, requires each agency to develop, maintain and update an organization-wide privacy program plan.

- The plan shall address the changes in federal privacy laws and policy that apply to the agency. (PM-18b)

</div>

#### Privacy program leadership role (PM-19)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall appoint a <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> with the authority, mission, accountability and resources to coordinate, develop and implement applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risk through the organization-wide privacy program. (PM-19)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall record the appointment in writing. (PM-19)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

[OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf) (July 28, 2016) requires each agency head to designate a Senior Agency Official for Privacy.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall be the Senior Agency Official for Privacy the agency head designates under OMB Circular A-130. (PM-19)

</div>

#### Dissemination of privacy program information (PM-20)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall maintain a privacy webpage on the organization's principal public website as the central source of information about the privacy program. (PM-20)
- The page shall give the public information about the organization's privacy activities and a way to contact the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span>. (PM-20a)
- The page shall make the organization's privacy practices and reports publicly available. (PM-20b)
- The page shall list a public email address or phone line for feedback and questions to the privacy office. (PM-20c)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

[OMB M-23-22](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/M-23-22-Delivering-a-Digital-First-Public-Experience.pdf), Delivering a Digital-First Public Experience (September 2023), requires each agency's privacy program page to be located at `www.[agency].gov/privacy`, as of September 2026.

- The privacy webpage shall be located at the address M-23-22 requires, `www.[agency].gov/privacy`. (PM-20)

</div>

#### Privacy policies on websites, applications and digital services (PM-20(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall ensure a privacy policy is posted on every external-facing website, mobile application and other digital service. (PM-20(1))
- Each privacy policy shall be written in plain language and organized so that it is easy to understand and navigate. (PM-20(1)(a))
- Each privacy policy shall give the public the information it needs to decide whether and how to interact with the organization. (PM-20(1)(b))
- Each privacy policy shall be updated whenever the organization makes a substantive change to the practices it describes, and shall show the date of the latest change. (PM-20(1)(c))

#### Accounting of disclosures (PM-21)

:::note[Guidance]
The retention period in PM-21b is fixed by NIST's control text, not a parameter. Keep the accounting where it can be searched by individual, so a request under PM-21c can be answered.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall ensure an accurate accounting is kept of each disclosure of personally identifiable information, recording the date, nature and purpose of the disclosure. (PM-21a.1)
- The accounting shall record the name and address, or other contact information, of the individual or organization that received the disclosure. (PM-21a.2)
- The accounting shall be kept for as long as the personally identifiable information is maintained or five years after the disclosure, whichever is longer. (PM-21b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall make the accounting available, on request, to the individual the information is about. (PM-21c)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

For records in a Privacy Act system of records, [5 U.S.C. § 552a(c)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title5-section552a&num=0&edition=prelim) sets this accounting. It excludes disclosures to agency employees who need the record for their duties (subsection (b)(1)) and disclosures the Freedom of Information Act requires (subsection (b)(2)). It does not require the accounting to be shown to the individual for law enforcement disclosures under subsection (b)(7).

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall keep the accounting of disclosures from each system of records as 5 U.S.C. § 552a(c) requires. (PM-21)

</div>

#### Personally identifiable information quality management (PM-22)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop and document organization-wide policies and procedures for reviewing personally identifiable information for accuracy, relevance, timeliness and completeness across the information life cycle. (PM-22a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop and document organization-wide policies and procedures for correcting or deleting inaccurate or outdated personally identifiable information. (PM-22b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop and document organization-wide policies and procedures for notifying individuals or other appropriate entities of corrected or deleted personally identifiable information. (PM-22c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop and document organization-wide policies and procedures for appeals of adverse decisions on correction or deletion requests. (PM-22d)

#### Data governance body (PM-23)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall establish a data governance body made up of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the roles of a Data Governance Body <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the chief data officer (chair), the chief information security officer, the senior privacy official, the records manager and the owners of major data sets</span></span>, with responsibility for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the responsibilities of a Data Governance Body <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: setting data governance policy, approving data sharing agreements, and resolving data quality and access issues</span></span>. (PM-23)

#### Data integrity board (PM-24)

:::note[Guidance]
A matching program is a computerized comparison of records about individuals, typically to establish or check eligibility for a benefit; the term comes from the U.S. Privacy Act. The steps for each matching program are in PT-8, in the [PII Processing and Transparency Policy](/templates/policies/pt/). If the organization runs no matching programs, keep the heading and record that decision in the program plan.
:::

- Where <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> conducts or takes part in a matching program, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall establish a data integrity board. (PM-24)
- The board shall review each proposal to conduct or take part in a matching program before the organization commits to it. (PM-24a)
- The board shall review, each year, every matching program the organization took part in. (PM-24b)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

The Privacy Act requires every agency that conducts or participates in a matching program to establish a Data Integrity Board, which reviews matching proposals and reviews all of the agency's matching programs each year ([5 U.S.C. § 552a(u)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title5-section552a&num=0&edition=prelim)).

- The data integrity board shall be established, staffed and run as 5 U.S.C. § 552a(u) requires. (PM-24)

</div>

#### Minimization of personally identifiable information used in testing, training and research (PM-25)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop, document and implement policies and procedures for using personally identifiable information in internal testing, training and research. (PM-25a)
- Internal testing, training and research shall use no more personally identifiable information than the purpose needs, and shall use synthetic or de-identified data wherever it serves the purpose. (PM-25b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall authorize each use of personally identifiable information for internal testing, training or research before it begins. (PM-25c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall review those policies <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for reviewing policies that address the use of personally identifiable information for internal testing, training, and research <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span> and update them <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for updating policies that address the use of personally identifiable information for internal testing, training, and research <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually, and whenever the review finds a change is needed</span></span>. (PM-25d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall review those procedures <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for reviewing procedures that address the use of personally identifiable information for internal testing, training, and research <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span> and update them <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for updating procedures that address the use of personally identifiable information for internal testing, training, and research <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually, and whenever the review finds a change is needed</span></span>. (PM-25d)

#### Complaint management (PM-26)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall implement a process for receiving and responding to complaints, concerns and questions from individuals about the organization's security and privacy practices. (PM-26)
- The process shall offer ways to file that are easy to use and readily accessible to the public. (PM-26a)
- The process shall tell individuals all the information they need to file a complaint successfully. (PM-26b)
- The process shall track each complaint so that it is reviewed within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period in which complaints (including concerns or questions) from individuals are to be reviewed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 5 business days</span></span> and addressed within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period in which complaints (including concerns or questions) from individuals are to be addressed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 30 days</span></span>. (PM-26c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall acknowledge receipt of each complaint, concern or question within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period for acknowledging the receipt of complaints <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 3 business days</span></span>. (PM-26d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall respond to each complaint, concern or question within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period for responding to complaints <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 30 days</span></span>. (PM-26e)

#### Privacy reporting (PM-27)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall develop <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: privacy reports <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: an annual privacy program report, summaries of privacy impact assessments, and breach reports</span></span>. (PM-27a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall disseminate the reports to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: privacy oversight bodies <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the board of directors or its audit committee, and regulators where law requires</span></span>, to demonstrate accountability with statutory, regulatory and policy privacy mandates. (PM-27a.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall disseminate the reports to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: officials responsible for monitoring privacy program compliance <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the senior leader, the chief information security officer and general counsel</span></span> and other personnel responsible for monitoring privacy program compliance. (PM-27a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall review and update the reports <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for reviewing and updating privacy reports <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>. (PM-27b)

#### Risk framing (PM-28)

:::note[Guidance]
Risk framing is the context every risk decision uses: the assumptions, constraints, priorities and risk tolerance. Most organizations record it as a section of the risk management strategy (PM-9).
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall identify and document the assumptions affecting risk assessment, risk response and risk monitoring. (PM-28a.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall identify and document the constraints affecting risk assessment, risk response and risk monitoring. (PM-28a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall identify and document the priorities and trade-offs the organization considers in managing risk. (PM-28a.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall set and document the organization's risk tolerance. (PM-28a.4)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall distribute the results of risk framing to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the personnel to receive the results of risk framing activities <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: authorizing officials, system owners, and the leaders of mission and business functions</span></span>. (PM-28b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update the risk framing <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for reviewing and updating risk framing considerations <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually, with the risk management strategy</span></span>. (PM-28c)

#### Risk management program leadership roles (PM-29)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall appoint a senior accountable official for risk management to align the organization's information security and privacy management processes with its strategic, operational and budgetary planning. (PM-29a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> shall establish a risk executive function to view and analyze risk from an organization-wide perspective and keep risk management consistent across the organization. (PM-29b)

#### Supply chain risk management strategy (PM-30)

:::note[Guidance]
The supply chain risk management strategy is organization-wide; the supply chain risk management plan (SR-2) applies it to systems. NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 describes both ([Update 1, November 2024](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/161/r1/upd1/final), current as of September 2026).
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall develop an organization-wide strategy for managing supply chain risks associated with the development, acquisition, maintenance and disposal of systems, system components and system services. (PM-30a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall implement the supply chain risk management strategy consistently across the organization. (PM-30b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review and update the supply chain risk management strategy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency for reviewing and updating the supply chain risk management strategy <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>, and whenever organizational changes require it. (PM-30c)

#### Suppliers of critical or mission-essential items (PM-30(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall identify and prioritize the suppliers of critical or mission-essential technologies, products and services. (PM-30(1))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall assess each of those suppliers for supply chain risk. (PM-30(1))

#### Continuous monitoring strategy (PM-31)

:::note[Guidance]
The organization-wide strategy sets the metrics and frequencies each system's continuous monitoring (CA-7) follows. The [Continuous Monitoring Strategy](/templates/plans/continuous-monitoring-strategy/) template holds both levels. NIST SP 800-137 ([September 2011](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/137/final), current as of September 2026) describes how to build it.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall develop an organization-wide continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring programs that follow it. (PM-31)
- The programs shall monitor these organization-wide metrics: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the metrics for organization-wide continuous monitoring <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: systems with a current authorization, plan of action items past due, vulnerabilities remediated within the required times, and staff with current security awareness training</span></span>. (PM-31a)
- The programs shall monitor control effectiveness <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequencies for monitoring <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: continuously for automated controls, and at least monthly for vulnerability, configuration and account data</span></span>. (PM-31b)
- The programs shall assess control effectiveness <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequencies for assessing control effectiveness <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a third of each system's controls each year, so every control is assessed at least every three years</span></span>. (PM-31b)
- The programs shall monitor the organization-wide metrics on an ongoing basis, as the strategy sets out. (PM-31c)
- The programs shall correlate and analyze the information that control assessments and monitoring produce. (PM-31d)
- The programs shall take response actions to address the results of that analysis. (PM-31e)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall report the security status of organizational systems to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the personnel or roles for reporting the security status of organizational systems to <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the senior leader and the authorizing officials</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to report the security status of organizational systems <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: monthly</span></span>. (PM-31f)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior privacy official</span> shall report the privacy status of organizational systems to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the personnel or roles for reporting the privacy status of organizational systems to <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the senior leader and the authorizing officials</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to report the privacy status of organizational systems <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly</span></span>. (PM-31f)

#### Purposing (PM-32)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall analyze <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the systems or system components supporting mission-essential services or functions <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the systems and components that support mission-essential functions, as the business impact analysis identifies them</span></span> to ensure their information resources are used consistently with their intended purpose. (PM-32)

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review this policy whenever the program plan is reviewed, and update it when the review finds a change is needed. (PM-1b)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal agencies, this policy carries out the agency-wide information security program required by the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554(b)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim)) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- The program plan shall carry out the agency-wide information security program that 44 U.S.C. § 3554(b) requires. (PM-1a)

</div>
